entries.test: Dated construction and operational records would establish how many of Abilene's eight buildings were functional on September 8, 2026.

entries.note: Abilene's completion is separately checkable, but the compound claim supplies no agreed test for reaching AGI.
The central assertion concerns the speakers' private intention to distract.
The proposition removes 'I think' and makes concentration risk an explicit cause rather than an associated concern.

entries.test: AI-sector valuations, financing, defaults and customer exposures over the following months and years would establish whether a broad unwind occurs amid widespread concentration risk.
entries.note: The horizon extends beyond the evaluation date without specifying a final year.

entries.test: Ramp's customer-spending data over the preceding three years would establish the top 1% revenue share and whether it improved.
entries.note: 'Hasn't improved' permits deterioration; 'unchanged' does not.

entries.test: Customer financial disclosures and funding histories would show whether the relevant startups require continuing venture funding to sustain their payments to the labs.
Representative enterprise spending surveys and financial disclosures would show whether most enterprises devote only small amounts to AI.

entries.note: 'Likely hundreds' is explicitly probabilistic. 'Many' also replaces the source's unspecified startup share.

entries.test: Pricing, usage allowances and model costs for the startups examined would establish whether nearly all allow token consumption substantially exceeding subscription payments.
entries.note: The proposition drops the restriction to cases Zitron has found.

entries.test: Subsequent financial disclosures, insolvencies or service terminations would establish whether these startup customers exhaust their ability to pay the labs because of their service economics.
Startup cash-flow statements and funding disclosures would show whether payments to AI labs depend on venture capital rather than operating cash generation.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph gives 'artificial' a concrete funding-based meaning.
Funding and run-rate figures are checkable separately; Harvey's hypothetical earlier demise is a counterfactual.

entries.test: The labs' customer revenue concentration, cash balances, expenses and financing disclosures would establish their financial dependence on VC-backed startup customers.
Model-launch revenue and usage data, compared across subsidized and unsubsidized customers, would show whether subsidies cause launch-related revenue surges.
entries.note: The proposition turns an explanation of how surges arise into a categorical claim about each launch.

entries.test: Customer concentration and startup funding disclosures would establish whether dependence on externally financed startup spending creates substantial revenue exposure for the labs.
entries.note: 'Not real revenue' refers in context to funding-dependent spending, rather than an accounting denial.

entries.test: If venture funding ceases, startup operating results and model offerings would show whether sustainability requires dropping these models and whether token costs dominate losses.
entries.note: The proposition weakens 'primary driver' to 'drive' and broadens 'these businesses' to AI startups generally.
Both 'likely' and 'could' express uncertainty. The proposition omits 'more,' which compares Anthropic spending with OpenAI spending.

entries.test: Customer cash flows, funding requirements and lab revenue-growth requirements would establish whether increased payments necessitate increasing external fundraising.
entries.note: The claim links inability to self-fund payments to the need for more fundraising.
Rational valuation is an evaluative judgment here. The proposition also omits the stated exception concerning investor incentives.

entries.test: Representative AI purchasing data classified by industry and startup profitability would establish whether tech firms comprise the vast majority outside unprofitable AI startups.
entries.note: 'Most' weakens 'vast majority,' and excluding all AI startups differs from excluding unprofitable ones.

entries.test: Cross-industry AI expenditure surveys and documented adoption trends would establish whether substantial spending outside tech is rare and lacks an evident reversal.

entries.note: Being a prime candidate for switching expresses potential, not a firm prediction that switching will occur.

entries.test: Revenue concentration, customer financing and spending-retention data would establish the share exposed to unstable funding or discretionary tech spending.
Annual compute contracts and customer-spending disclosures excluding OpenAI and Anthropic would establish total demand and Jane Street's and NVIDIA's shares.
entries.note: The proposition presents an explicitly personal estimate as an unqualified figure.

entries.test: If the labs cannot take their committed capacity, replacement contracts would establish whether other customers absorb that compute at comparable scale.
entries.note: The surrounding argument supplies the contingency that the labs cannot buy the capacity.

entries.test: Disclosed compute agreements would establish whether the labs' commitments exceed $1.3 trillion and materially exceed their available financing and operating cash generation.
entries.note: The mortgage analogy is supported by a concrete claim about inadequately financed obligations.

entries.test: Annual financial disclosures or documented financial reporting for both labs would establish their annual losses.
Published 2027 revenue estimates and the labs' financing and customer cash-flow disclosures would establish the forecast amount and its dependence on externally funded growth.
entries.note: 'Largely VC-funded' is stronger than 'many of whom are funded by venture capital.' The claim concerns existing expectations and their financing dependencies.

entries.test: Contract payment schedules and monthly capacity commissioning records would establish whether substantial new payments start in 2027 and increase month after month.

entries.note: This recommends how the commitments should be regarded.
The compound includes the explicitly uncertain 'I doubt.' The proposition also drops 'dramatically' from the expected annual expansion.

entries.test: The labs' contractual compute bills falling due during calendar 2027 would establish whether the total reaches $200 billion.

entries.note: The degree of resemblance between the two financing episodes has no shared decisive test.

entries.test: A representative content analysis of contemporary AI reporting would establish how frequently positive financial figures appear while material negative figures are omitted.
entries.note: The source says reporting 'mostly' does this; the proposition attributes the behavior to nearly all reporting.
Concentration can be compared, but 'simpler' and 'easier to see' lack a shared test for the compound assertion.
This is a probabilistic inference about Microsoft's current expectations for future revenue.
The larger payment amount is explicitly presented as something that 'could' occur.

entries.test: OpenAI's published compute-spending projections and annual expenditures through 2030 would establish whether they support spending of at least $250 billion a year.
entries.note: 'Implies' is firmer than 'suggests.' The source nevertheless advances a concrete numerical spending expectation.
The spike is expressly a possibility.

entries.test: The labs' growth through September 2029, profitability, cumulative financing and payment performance would establish whether meeting their obligations requires the stated growth and funding thresholds.
entries.note: Profitability is required 'at some point,' not explicitly within three years.
This attributes a particular private rationale to hyperscaler decision-makers.
The source explicitly says 'very unlikely.'

entries.test: OpenAI's 2025 financial results and quarterly operating results through Q2 2026 would establish the expenses, revenue and deterioration to a negative 183% operating margin.

entries.note: 'I assume' presents the underwriting allegation as conjecture.

entries.test: Available liquidity, contractual payment schedules and upfront fees would establish the labs' payment capacity and whether low initial charges explain their ability to keep current.
entries.note: The assertion includes an explicit causal explanation for keeping up with payments.

entries.test: Financing requirements and compute payment schedules as contracted capacity begins operating would establish whether capital needs rise sharply in large increments.
entries.note: Commencement is treated as an expected event, rather than a hypothetical antecedent.

entries.test: NVIDIA sales disclosures and its customers' downstream compute revenues would establish how much of its customer demand ultimately depends on OpenAI and Anthropic.
AI revenue disclosures and direct and intermediary compute contracts for the named providers would establish the share attributable to OpenAI and Anthropic.
Backlog contracts, reciprocal investments and public promotional statements would establish whether providers finance their own booked demand and market it as independent demand.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a concrete meaning for the characterization.

entries.test: GPU and data-center costs compared with purchasers' cash generation, liquidity and borrowing would establish whether continued purchases require substantial debt outside Microsoft.
entries.note: 'Nearly no company' weakens 'nobody' other than Microsoft. The claim causally attributes financing constraints to GPU prices.

entries.test: GPU deployment contracts and provider revenue attribution would establish whether almost all returns and most new capacity depend on the two labs.
entries.note: The proposition omits the assertion that each provider builds capacity mostly or entirely for the labs.

entries.test: Hyperscaler compute revenues, capital expenditure returns and NVIDIA purchase patterns would establish whether payments from the two labs underpin the stated investment and vendor revenues.
Microsoft's FY2026 AI revenue breakdown would establish total AI revenue and the portion generated independently of OpenAI.
entries.note: 'Showing' strengthens the source's 'suggests' concerning underlying demand.

entries.test: Following an AI-sector collapse, bankruptcy filings and financial disclosures would establish whether it causes either company to fail and how Broadcom's revenues depend on the labs.
entries.note: The source rules out bankruptcy caused by the bubble bursting; the proposition rules out bankruptcy when it bursts, regardless of cause.
'Look fine' supplies no shared measure of conditions or whose perception matters.
The supply-chain dependence is substantive, rather than empty rhetoric. The proposition removes 'maybe' from the estimated customer count.
A correction is asserted firmly, but its exceeding the dot-com collapse is explicitly qualified by 'likely.'
